strings.name: David Baker
strings.summary: David Baker extended protein-folding research toward designing new proteins from scratch. His teams developed computational methods including Rosetta and tested whether designed molecules formed the intended structures and functions. The work combines biochemistry, computing and machine learning to explore new enzymes, binding proteins and materials. He received half the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for computational protein design; medical applications require their own validation.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Designing proteins from scratch

strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Shared computational methods
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Advanced Rosetta and later learning methods for structure prediction, molecular design and collaboration.
